name: Newsletter sign-up with double opt-in
problem: Visitors can join the newsletter from the footer, but nothing confirms the address, so typos and other people's addresses end up on the list.
summary: The footer form sends a confirmation email. The address joins the list only when its link is opened within 48 hours.

acs.text: Submitting the footer form sends one confirmation email and shows `Check your inbox`.
Opening the link within 48 hours adds the address to the list; after 48 hours it shows `This link has expired`.
An address already on the list gets no second email and sees the same message.

subtasks.title: Add the pending sign-ups table
subtasks.tierWhy: A migration that copies the existing tables' pattern.
subtasks.approach: A `pending_signups` table holding the address, a token hash and the expiry.

subtasks.title: Send the confirmation email on sign-up
subtasks.tierWhy: A business rule with three branches: new, pending and already subscribed.
subtasks.approach: The form handler creates or refreshes the pending row and sends the email through the existing mailer; a known address gets the same reply and no email.

questions.question: Resend the email when a pending address signs up again?
questions.recommend: Resend, at most once an hour

options.name: Resend, at most once an hour
cons: One more rate limit to test

options.name: Never resend
cons: A lost email leaves the visitor stuck for 48 hours

subtasks.title: Confirm the address from the email link
subtasks.tierWhy: Raised from Medium: the first token approach could not be revoked.
subtasks.approach: A confirmation route that checks the token, moves the address onto the list and deletes the pending row.

proof.what: Sign up, open the link, then replay it after moving the clock past 48 hours; the log shows `newsletter.confirmed` once and `newsletter.link_expired` once.

questions.question: Signed token in the link, or a random token stored hashed?

options.name: Signed token
options.summary: The link carries the address and expiry, signed.
cons: Puts the address in the URL

options.name: Random token, stored hashed
options.summary: The link carries only a random value.

questions.question: Where does an expired link send the visitor?
questions.recommend: Back to the sign-up form, prefilled

options.name: Back to the sign-up form, prefilled
A plain expiry page
pros: No personal data on the page
cons: The visitor has to find the form

subtasks.title: Document the sign-up flow
subtasks.approach: Describe the flow and the expiry in the newsletter docs page.

proof.what: Sign up a new, a pending and a known address against the local stack; the mail log shows two emails and the replies are identical.

complete.summary: Only addresses whose owner opened the link within 48 hours are on the list.
outcome: A Playwright spec for the happy path and the expired link
complete.proving: P1 proves the sign-up branches locally; subtask 3 replays the confirmation and the expiry.

escalated.reason: Signed tokens could not be revoked; the developer agreed a stored token before the approach changed.
